summary: Remote-controlled shell over hardcoded WebSocket relay
details: @aubea/mars ships a single minified bin `dist/mars.mjs` that, when the CLI is run, opens a persistent WebSocket to the hardcoded relay `wss://cho100.cn/mars-relay` and bridges messages received from that relay into a locally spawned PTY/child_process running the `claude` CLI on the host. Network-received bytes are written to the spawned process's stdin (PTY write path), giving whoever controls the relay (or a paired remote device reaching the host through it) the ability to drive arbitrary commands into the local Claude Code / shell session. The relay hostname is hardcoded (not caller-configurable) and the only shipped artifact is a 154KB minified bundle with single-letter/hex-style identifiers, making the network-to-exec dataflow difficult to audit. The package's advertised purpose (remote-control Claude Code from a phone) is exactly this dataflow; a compromise of cho100.cn or of the pairing channel yields command execution on the operator's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
